subject: Access lanes, MAP & provisioning commitments for evaluation kit
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@acme-retail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Request: evaluation kit + MAP and timelines

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers look promising. Our evaluation team is ready to run a short pilot but we need a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a clear provisioning checklist before we can spin up the sandbox. Specifically can you provide: 

- A MAP with milestones and handoff points (provisioning, acceptance gate, takedown).
- A sample prompt pack and a small testcase corpus to validate quality.
- Any usage constraints / license language (ephemeral access, no redistribution, retention).
- Expected timeline from signature to provisioning.

We’re aiming for a two-week evaluation window and want acceptance criteria defined up front (pass/fail, metric thresholds). Please include a point of contact for Security so we can get the KBA answered quickly.

I’ll loop in Tom from Legal once we have a draft.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Grant
Lead ML Architect, Acme Retail

Attachments: none
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@acme-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evaluation kit + MAP and timelines

Hi Sophie — great to connect. Appreciate the clarity on scope. I attached a draft MAP (MAP-access-lanes-v1.pdf) and a starter prompt pack + sample testcases we typically provision for retail pilots. Highlighted items in the MAP: provisioning SLA, acceptance gates, and usage guardrails. Short summary below: 

- Provisioning: sandbox + data access lanes provisioned after MAP signature via DocuSign (link in email). ETA 48 hours post-signature.
- Access model: ephemeral credentials, per-user token limits, IP allowlist option for Acme.
- Retention / take-down: default 90 days from provisioning unless extended by agreement.
- Acceptance: run provided testcases_sample.csv + your in-house probes; success = >= 80% pass on primary classification tasks and no regression on latency beyond 25% of baseline.
- Usage constraints: no redistribution, no dataset exfiltration, no re-bundling of the prompt pack, and no inclusion in third-party benchmarks without express consent.

Next steps I propose: I’ll loop Karthik to confirm the security checklist and Connor for the sandbox provisioning playbook. If legal has redlines, Tom can send them back and we’ll incorporate. If you’re comfortable I can start a DocuSign envelope for the MAP and we’ll hold provisioning until the signed MAP is received.

Attached: MAP-access-lanes-v1.pdf, promptpack_trial_v2.zip, testcases_sample.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0192

---
On 2027-05-09 09:02, Sophie Grant wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers look promising...
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-10T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Request: evaluation kit + MAP and timelines

Folks — quick technical addendum for the MAP before we send to Acme: 

- Network: we’ll provision sandbox within a dedicated VPC subnet. We can enforce an IP allowlist and set up a small outbound-only NAT for telemetry.
- Keys & audit: customer keys via bring-your-own-KMS (optional); we will capture per-request access logs (S3 + CloudTrail style) for the duration of the evaluation. Logs are retained for 120 days by default unless the MAP specifies otherwise.
- Artifact delivery: promptpack_trial_v2.zip will be hosted on ephemeral presigned URLs (expiry 72 hrs) until ingestion. We can also do direct SFTP if Acme prefers.
- Token limits: sensible defaults (concurrent sessions: 5 per user, 10k tokens/day per company) — adjustable per negotiation.
- Sandbox provisioning ETA: once DocuSign is complete we will schedule within 48 hours; if legal requests additional SCA we may need up to 72 hours.

I’ll prepare a one-page security annex to attach (DSP-SLA.csv) and finalize the KBA responses.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@acme-retail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Vega <legal@acme-retail.com>, eval-team@acme-retail.com
Date: 2027-05-11T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access lanes, MAP & provisioning commitments for evaluation kit

Thanks Marissa + team — this is helpful. A few notes from Acme: 

1) Retention: our security team prefers 120 days for access logs and artifacts rather than 90. Can Redwood accommodate 120 days?
2) Prompt pack usage: we want language confirming prompts/testcases are provided only for evaluation and cannot be used to train internal models outside the evaluation environment.
3) Acceptance criteria: can we add a small hold-out set (we’ll provide 1k hold-out lines) to validate no leakage?

Tom from Legal is cc’d — he will send any formal redlines. He also asked for a short Data Use Checklist; attaching the checklist we use internally to speed reviews.

If the above is acceptable we can sign the MAP next week. Also please confirm whether token limits can be raised if we extend the pilot.

Thanks,
Sophie

Attachments: Acme-Data-Use-Checklist.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@acme-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access lanes, MAP & provisioning commitments for evaluation kit

Hi Sophie / Tom — quick confirmation after internal alignment: 

- Retention: we’ll set access log + artifact retention to 120 days as requested. We’ll note that in the MAP and in the security annex.
- Prompt pack usage: we’ll add explicit non-training language — prompts and testcases provided remain under ephemeral evaluation license and may not be used to train models outside the sandbox.
- Hold-out set: happy to accept Acme’s 1k hold-out lines; we’ll include an acceptance step using that set in the MAP.
- Token limits: adjustable — we’ll start with the defaults (10k tokens/day) and can increase after a short usage review; we’ll document the process in the MAP.
- Provisioning timeline: 48–72 hours after DocuSign-completed signature and receipt of KBA answers.

I’ve started a DocuSign envelope for the MAP here: https://docusign.com/link/embedded/ACME-MAP-2027 (also attached as docusign_acme_map_link.txt). If legal has redlines, please send them as annotated PDF or a tracked Word doc and we’ll respond by EOD Friday.

Once the MAP is signed we’ll provision the sandbox and hand over the prompt pack ingestion guide to Connor for onboarding.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: docusign_acme_map_link.txt
